policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere הַהִיא and ketiv ההוא are the two orthographies of the same demonstrative attached to הָעִיר, and both are read as the feminine 'that' agreeing with the city. The ASV has only 'the inhabitants of that city', which renders the demonstrative identically either way, and the single mapped note is a hebrew_gloss on 'destroying it utterly' that says nothing about the pronoun's spelling. Nothing in the English distinguishes them, so both readings stand and the qere base fallback carries the projection.
